Title: Brent Crude oil hits highest since April 2024 as Middle East conflict escalates

Summary: 
On March 6, 2026, crude oil prices surged to their highest levels since April 2024 as escalating Middle East conflict disrupted energy supplies. According to reports, Brent Crude climbed approximately 20% this week and traded over 3% higher at around $89 per barrel on Friday, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) surged roughly 25% to about $86 per barrel. The sharp rally was triggered by US and Israeli strikes on Iran last weekend, prompting Iran to block oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, a route carrying about one-fifth of the world's daily oil supply. Qatar's energy minister warned in an interview with the Financial Times that if the conflict continues, Gulf producers might shut down exports within weeks, potentially pushing oil prices to $150 per barrel. The disruption has spread to major energy-producing regions, forcing several refineries and liquefied natural gas plants to shut down. Consequently, European stocks declined and US stock futures slipped as investors feared higher energy prices would increase inflation and slow economic growth.

Published date: March 06 2026, 12:59
